title: Spot the principle: matching behaviours to principles
blurb: Recognize which of the seven principles a described action applies, including the near misses examiners love.
question: A project board sets a cost tolerance of plus or minus 5% for the next stage. Is that manage by stages or manage by exception?

teach.h: Find the idea behind the action
teach.body: Exam questions describe an action and ask which principle it applies. Don't match on surface words such as 'stage' or 'product'. Ask what the action is really for: a reason to continue, lessons, people and relationships, decision points, limits of authority, defining outputs, or fitting the method. Each of those points to exactly one principle.

head: If the action is about...
...the principle is
rows: Reason to start or continue; stopping; best-value option
Seeking, recording, sharing lessons; social learning
Agreed roles; business, user, supplier; building relationships
Decision points; one stage at a time; stage plan for the near term
Tolerances; escalating forecast breaches; local decisions
Defining outputs and their quality before the work
Fitting processes, roles, products, terms and controls to the project

rows.label: In planning
values: Detailed plan for the next stage

teach.caption: An action can happen AT a stage boundary and still apply another principle: setting stage tolerances is manage by exception.

head: People behaviour
Principle
rows: Deciding at the most local level with the knowledge
Reviewing how people interact at stage ends
Co-creating products with users and suppliers
teach.caption: Based on the manual's 'people central to the method' guidance (3.5.1) and the wording of the roles principle (2.3).

teach.body: Tailor to suit the project means fitting the method to the project's environment, size, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability and level of risk. Changing terminology, merging documents, adding a coach role or adjusting how often and how formally reports are made are all tailoring. Dropping a principle or breaking a role rule is never tailoring.

teach.h: Worked scenario: one project, seven principles
teach.body: Brightwater Leisure Trust is refurbishing its pool changing rooms. Watch project manager Ellie Fraser's week: each action applies a different principle. Learn the pattern, not the scenario.

items: Checks the refurbishment still beats doing the minimum after a price rise: ensure continued business justification.
Reads the lessons report from the gym refit: learn from experience.
Introduces the contractor's site lead to the lifeguard team: define roles, responsibilities and relationships.
Prepares the detailed plan for the next stage only: manage by stages.
Gives the tiling team a plus or minus three-day tolerance: manage by exception.
Agrees slip-resistance criteria for the floor before ordering tiles: focus on products.
Uses the Trust's own term 'job sheet' for work packages: tailor to suit the project.

teach.text: Classic traps: (1) Setting tolerances, even stage tolerances, is manage by exception, not manage by stages. (2) Defining what is in scope is focus on products; the allowed variation (scope tolerance) is manage by exception. (3) Social learning is learn from experience; local decision-making is manage by exception. (4) A compulsory project still applies ensure continued business justification.

items: Ask what the action is for, not which words it contains.
Stages = decision points; exception = tolerances and escalation; products = defining outputs and quality.
Tailoring adapts the method; it never removes a principle.
People behaviours map to principles too (social learning, local decisions, co-creation).

summary: You can now identify which principle a described action applies by asking what the action is for. You can also separate the classic near misses: manage by stages, manage by exception and focus on products, learn from experience versus local decision-making, and genuine tailoring versus dropping a principle.

A.q: A project manager prepares a detailed plan for the next stage, because later work cannot yet be planned in detail. Which principle is being applied?
A.why: Planning the near future in detail through a stage plan, under a high-level project plan, applies manage by stages.

whyNot.1: Manage by exception concerns tolerances and escalation, not the planning horizon.
whyNot.2: Focus on products concerns defining products and their quality.
whyNot.3: Tailoring adapts the method; detailed stage planning is part of the method itself.

A.q: A project manager gives a team manager a work package tolerance of plus or minus three days. Which principle is being applied?
A.why: Setting tolerances to define limits of delegated authority applies manage by exception.

whyNot.0: Manage by stages concerns stage-by-stage planning and decision points.
whyNot.2: Focus on products concerns defining products and their quality.
whyNot.3: The action sets a limit of authority; it does not define roles or relationships.

A.q: Before design work starts, the team agrees what each deliverable must contain and how its quality will be checked. Which principle is being applied?
A.why: Defining products and their quality before doing the work applies focus on products.

whyNot.0: The action defines outputs; it does not test whether the project is worth continuing.
whyNot.1: Manage by exception sets tolerances; this defines the products themselves.
whyNot.3: No lessons are being sought or applied here.

B.q: A team new to this kind of work contacts two other organizations that ran similar projects to hear what went wrong and right. Which principle is being applied?
B.why: Seeking lessons from others, especially external sources for a novel project, applies learn from experience.

whyNot.0: The contact is to gain lessons, not to define roles or build project relationships.
whyNot.1: Nothing about the method is being adapted.
whyNot.2: Manage by stages concerns stage-by-stage planning and decisions.

B.q: On a small, low-risk project, the board agrees to receive short highlight reports by email each month instead of formal fortnightly reports. Which principle is being applied?
B.why: Adjusting the frequency and formality of reports to the project's scale and risk is tailoring.

whyNot.0: Highlight reports are produced either way; the change adapts their format and frequency.
whyNot.2: The stage structure has not changed.
whyNot.3: The change is not driven by recording or applying lessons.

B.q: A software firm's account director is appointed senior supplier so the supplier interest is represented on the board. Which principle is being applied?
B.why: Representing the business, user and supplier interests through defined roles applies define roles, responsibilities and relationships.

whyNot.1: The appointment is about representation, not justification.
whyNot.3: No tolerance or escalation is involved.

C.q: To meet a new safety regulation, a project compares three ways of complying and chooses the best-value one. Which principle is applied, and why?
options: Focus on products, because each option defines different outputs
Manage by exception, because each option sets a cost tolerance
Ensure continued business justification, because the option is justified
Tailor to suit the project, because compliance changes the method
C.why: Even compulsory projects need justification of the chosen option, so choosing the best-value way to comply applies ensure continued business justification.

whyNot.0: The comparison is about value for money, not defining products.
whyNot.1: Comparing options is not setting tolerances.
whyNot.3: Choosing a compliance option does not adapt the PRINCE2 method.

C.q:
Which two statements are correct?
1. Setting tolerances for a stage applies manage by stages.
2. Defining the products that are in scope applies focus on products.
3. Escalating a forecast breach of stage tolerance applies manage by exception.
4. Merging two management products applies manage by exception.
C.why: Defining products in scope is focus on products (2), and escalating a forecast tolerance breach is manage by exception (3).

whyNot.0: Statement 1 is false: setting tolerances, even for a stage, is manage by exception.
whyNot.1: Both are false: tolerances are manage by exception, and merging products is tailoring.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: merging management products is tailoring.

C.q: A team manager resequences tasks inside her work package without involving the project manager, because she has the knowledge and it stays within tolerance. Which principle is being applied?
C.why: Making decisions at the most local level where the knowledge resides, within tolerance, applies manage by exception.

whyNot.0: No lesson is being sought or shared; the point is where the decision is made.
whyNot.1: The action happens within a work package, not at a stage decision point.
whyNot.2: Roles are already defined; the action uses the authority delegated to her.

reteach.title: Seven questions, seven principles
reteach.question: If you could ask only one question about an action, which question would reveal its principle?

blocks.body: Turn each principle into a question. Is it still worth doing? (justification). What have we or others learned? (experience). Who does what, and how do they work together? (roles and relationships). When do we decide? (stages). How much freedom does each level have? (exception). What exactly are we delivering? (products). Does the method fit this project? (tailoring). The question an action answers is its principle.

blocks.text: An action taken at a stage boundary is not automatically manage by stages: check what it is for.

explain.body: Manage by stages gives the board review and decision points at each stage end, with the project planned and controlled one stage at a time.

test.q: Which principle is most directly linked with review and decision points for the board?
test.why: Stages provide review and decision points so the board can assess viability at defined intervals.

whyNot.0: Manage by exception covers tolerances and escalation between decision points.
whyNot.1: Focus on products covers defining and delivering products.

explain.body: Setting a tolerance is manage by exception, even when the tolerance is for a stage and is set at a stage boundary.

test.q: A project board sets a time tolerance of plus or minus two weeks for the next stage. Which principle is this?
test.why: Defining tolerances sets limits of delegated authority: manage by exception.

whyNot.0: The action happens at a stage boundary, but setting tolerances is manage by exception.
whyNot.3: Setting tolerances is part of the method, not an adaptation of it.

explain.body: Writing what a product must be, including its quality specifications, is focus on products. The permitted variation around targets is manage by exception.

test.q: A team writes quality specifications for each product before work starts. Which principle is applied?
test.why: Defining products and their quality before the work is focus on products.

whyNot.0: Manage by exception sets tolerances rather than defining products.
whyNot.1: Manage by stages concerns decision points and stage plans.

explain.body: Tailoring adapts processes, practices, roles, management products, terminology and the frequency or formality of controls to the project.

test.q: Which action applies tailor to suit the project?
options: Using the client's own name for work packages
Setting work package tolerances for a team
Recording a new lesson in the lessons log
test.why: Using the organization's own terminology is a recognized form of tailoring.

whyNot.1: Setting tolerances applies manage by exception.
whyNot.2: Recording lessons applies learn from experience.
whyNot.3: Agreeing quality criteria applies focus on products.
